parameters.name: model.trophic_transfer_efficiency
parameters.note: Midpoint of the 5-20% energy transfer efficiency between trophic levels (the textbook range following Lindeman 1942; from memory, verify). The midpoint is a choice, not a measurement.

parameters.name: model.trophic_amplification_exponent
parameters.note: No source: damps the pyramid ratio to 1.6-4.1× amplification for trophic levels 1-3.

parameters.name: model.keystone_edge_multiplier
parameters.note: No source: outgoing edge strengths of a collapsed keystone agent are multiplied by this factor.

parameters.name: carbon_price.year0
parameters.note: Social cost of carbon. The 2020-emissions value is used as the year-0 price: EPA's own path gives about $215 for 2026 emissions, so year-0 carbon damage is understated by about 13%. 2020 euros, no inflation adjustment.
parameters.source: US EPA (2023), Report on the Social Cost of Greenhouse Gases, Table ES.1: $190/tCO2 (2020 emissions, 2020 USD, 2% near-term rate), at the ECB 2020 average rate of 1.1422 USD/EUR

parameters.name: carbon_price.growth
parameters.note: 60-year average of a decelerating path (1.6%/yr in 2020-2050, 1.2%/yr in 2030-2080).

parameters.name: resource.area_ha
parameters.note: Units / reference density of 100 trees/ha. Chosen so the per-tree absorption gives ~1.8 t CO2/ha/yr.

parameters.name: resource.unit_value
parameters.note: Revenue per holm oak felled (one-off). Rated Medium in the case docstring, but no market source is cited.
parameters.source: owner specification (case docstring), no external source

parameters.name: resource.safe_threshold_ratio
parameters.note: Safe extraction threshold, lower than temperate forest for drought and fire (stated rationale, no cited source); under the area_loss damage model (Step 8d.1) the depletion beyond which the REMAINING resource starts to degrade; below it each hectare lost costs its average value.
parameters.source: owner specification (case docstring), no external source

parameters.name: agents.annual_value_per_ha
parameters.note: Every agent; the dependency weights split it. Figure partly from memory, to be checked against the paper (Step 8); 2007 Int$ used as € with no currency or price-year conversion; a global woodland mean, not a Mediterranean holm-oak valuation.
parameters.source: de Groot et al. (2012), Ecosystem Services 1:50-61: woodlands Int$1,588/ha/yr; minus climate regulation Int$7 (SM Table 9.1)

parameters.name: damage.threshold_logistic_steepness
parameters.note: Degradation of the REMAINING resource past the safe threshold (damage model area_loss, Step 8d.1, as for Posidonia): zero up to the threshold, then a logistic with its inflection 15% into the post-threshold span, the same curve for every agent except Fire & Microclimate Regulation. The damage of each agent is D + (1 - D) x degradation, so its slope at small losses is exactly 1 (each hectare lost costs its average value) and the curve shapes only the threshold behaviour. Not fitted to field data (calibration regime B). Monte Carlo range 6-18, uniform (Step 8e.4, as Posidonia: a judgement; the placeholder x/÷3 gave 4-36).

parameters.name: damage.threshold_exponential_base
parameters.note: Degradation of Fire & Microclimate Regulation past the safe threshold (area_loss, Step 8d.1): zero up to the threshold, then exponential over the post-threshold span (fire feedback, no plateau): (base^((D - t)/(1 - t)) - 1)/(base - 1); not fitted to fire data. Monte Carlo range 1.5-3 (x0.75 to x1.5, Step 8e.4): the base must stay above 1 for a growing curve, and the placeholder x/÷3 (0.67-6) put a third of the draws at or below 1, which validation rejects.

parameters.name: agent[Mycorrhizal Fungi].keystone_threshold
parameters.note: Health below which the agent's outgoing edges double; hand-set, no source. Monte Carlo range 0.15-0.45, uniform (Step 8e.4, Posidonia's +-0.15: a judgement; the placeholder x/÷3 reached 0.9-1.0, where the keystone boost would fire at almost any damage).

parameters.name: agent[Pollinators & Insects].keystone_threshold
parameters.note: Health below which the agent's outgoing edges double; hand-set, no source. Monte Carlo range 0.25-0.55, uniform (Step 8e.4, Posidonia's +-0.15: a judgement; the placeholder x/÷3 reached 0.9-1.0, where the keystone boost would fire at almost any damage).

parameters.name: edge[Mycorrhizal Fungi → Canopy Trees].strength
parameters.note: Hand-set placeholder strength. Monte Carlo range (Step 8e.4): x0.5 to x1.176. The incoming strengths into Canopy Trees sum to 0.850 of the in-degree cap of 1 (keystone boosts included), so the edges into it can rise only by x1.176 together before a draw breaks the cap; their documented values are therefore the top of their range (x1.176), not its middle. Drawn values are never rescaled.

parameters.name: pricing.anchor[Mycorrhizal Fungi]
parameters.note: EXPERIMENTAL pricing (quarantined). A market-based value (Step 8d.6): food (provisioning; in Mediterranean woodland largely wild mushrooms, the fruiting bodies of mycorrhizal fungi) Int$, Int$52/ha/yr x 100 ha, a global woodlands mean, not a site valuation; for scale, Catalan pine forests yield ~14 kg/ha/yr of marketed mushrooms (de-Miguel et al. 2014, Forest Ecology and Management 330:218-227, doi:10.1016/j.foreco.2014.07.014)
parameters.source: de Groot et al. (2012), Ecosystem Services 1:50-61, doi:10.1016/j.ecoser.2012.07.005, Table 2 (Int$/ha/yr, 2007 price level, used as EUR at face value): woodlands, food (provisioning; in Mediterranean woodland largely wild mushrooms, the fruiting bodies of mycorrhizal fungi) Int$ 52; Table 1: 118 of the database's 133 food estimates are direct market prices

parameters.source: de Groot et al. (2012), Ecosystem Services 1:50-61, doi:10.1016/j.ecoser.2012.07.005, Table 2 (Int$/ha/yr, 2007 price level, used as EUR at face value): woodlands, pollination Int$ 31; Table 1: 2 of its 3 pollination estimates are factor income/production function values (crop output at market prices)

pricing.derived_prices_note: No anchor of their own: each price is derived from the anchored agents upstream through the placeholder edge strengths (Step 8c.6).
pricing.note: EXPERIMENTAL (decision D4, C8): endogenous pricing is quarantined. Every price is certified convergent (a run that cannot be certified fails instead of falling back to static values), but the formulation counts upstream value once per dependent agent and prices the whole loss at the end-state scarcity price, and most shipped anchors are placeholders. Do not use these figures as estimates.
